title: Gold Shoes
content:
For my birthday Dida gave me gold shoes.

In the card she wrote: “These are magic shoes. They are made of jute, the golden grass that grows in your motherland. They will take you where you want to go and always bring you home. And, wherever you may go, you will leave a beautiful footprint.”

I did not like the shoes. They were not colorful and did not make me any taller. The other kids had shoes with lights and bounce. I had jute shoes.

But then one day, walking home from school, I lost my way and had to turn back. As I walked, I saw my footprints on the road, leading me back to where I had taken the wrong turn.

My footprint was a little house with flowers all around. I understood why Grandma gave me these shoes as a gift! My shoes have beautiful soles and they will always take me home. I love my gold walking shoes!

NoteOur earth gives us everything we need to live - water, food, air, and materials to make clothes and homes. Jute, known as the Gold of Bengal, has a very small carbon footprint and can be used to make absolutely anything from shoes to boats to tea.

title: No Ordinary Herbs
content:
Jingle, jangle! Every time Tinuk saw children riding their bikes to school, she got more excited about saving up money. She wanted to have a bike like theirs. In a year, Tinuk would study at a junior high school that was quite far from her house. It would be easier for her to ride a bicycle there. Hopefully Mom could give Tinuk more pocket money.

However, this afternoon Mom came home with a lot of leftover herbal drinks. Oh no, Mom would be at a loss if she couldn’t sell all her herbal drinks. She wouldn’t have any extra pocket money to give Tinuk. Hmm, maybe Tinuk could help her out.

Tinuk decided to bring the herbal drinks with her to the field. She would sell the herbs to her friends before they played football. Tinuk needed to move the herbal drink bottles out of the basket. She couldn’t carry the basket like Mom could.

“Get your herbal drinks here! Herbs for a healthy body,” Tinuk announced. Tinuk’s friends came up to her. However, they didn’t like herbal drinks that taste bitter. They only wanted sweet herbs. One friend even jokingly asked for a strawberry-flavored one. Hearing that, an idea popped into Tinuk’s head.

Tinuk would make different flavored herbal drinks. Most importantly, they must all be sweet. Tinuk added a lot of cinnamon to the turmeric mix, but…

Yuck! It tasted bitter and smelled strange. There wasn’t even a bit of sweetness to it. It turns out that cinnamon isn’t sweet after all. Maybe the measurements needed to be changed? Tinuk mixed in other fragrant ingredients like lemongrass, ginger, and pandan.

Why is the kitchen such a mess?” Mother asked. “I’m making herbal drinks, Mom,” answered Tinuk. “Have a taste.”

“What kind of herb is this? It’s too fragrant and too sweet.” Mother wrinkled her nose. “It’s rice with aromatic ginger. I mixed in a lot of pandan leaves, so it smells good,” Tinuk answered.

Hmm, that meant Tinuk used too much sugar and pandan. She needed to try other flavor combinations.

However, there was only a little bit of sugar and cinnamon left. Tinuk felt guilty. Mom must not have much money left to buy more herbal ingredients. Tinuk would use some of her own savings to buy more brown sugar and cinnamon.

While waiting in line at the stall, Tinuk saw a shelf filled with various packaged herbs. There was even a picture of a woman who resembled Mom on the packaging. How interesting.

Wow, so many people were buying this drink. Was it because it’s sold in a small bottle? The small picture and name of the drink written on the bottle made it even more interesting. Another new idea popped into Tinuk’s head.

As soon as she got home, Tinuk immediately looked for small bottles. However, she could only find her water bottle.

Tinuk used her savings again to buy plastic bottles. She didn’t mind, as long as more people would buy Mom’s herbal drinks.

Now was time for Tinuk to draw a picture for the bottle. What should she draw? Tinuk wasn’t good at drawing Mom. Oh, she just thought of something. Tinuk would draw Mom’s silhouette instead. Underneath, she wrote down a phone number and the brand name. Tinuk gave it the name Mrs. Marni’s Herbal Drinks. That way people would know that these were the same herbal drinks her mom usually carried around.

Tinuk then photocopied the logo at a photocopy store. She cut out the logos and stuck them on to the bottles, but she wasn’t done yet. There was something else Tinuk needed to do.

Tinuk needed to make a sign to put up in front of her house. Again, Tinuk used her savings to buy cardboard paper and colored markers.

Instead of saving up her money, she had ended up spending more. Tinuk must try her best to make this work.

There was only one more thing left to do. Tinuk had to promote Mom’s herbal drinks so that more people would buy it. They needed to know that Mom’s herbal drinks now come in branded bottles. “If you want to order herbal drinks, you can contact this number,” Tinuk said as she handed out fliers.

"Can I have a bottle of herbs?” Hurray! The first customers had arrived.

More and more customers were right behind them. Not only did Mom’s herbal concoctions sell, but Tinuk’s did too. “Can I order some over the phone to send to a friend?” someone asked. Of course!

Almost every day, Tinuk added more money into her savings. Before she knew it, she had saved up enough money to buy a bike!

“You can borrow my bike to sell your herbs, Mom,” Tinuk smiled.

title: When is Mom Coming Home?
content:
Mom was going to Jakarta to work as a babysitter. While Mom was away, Alia and Bagas were staying with Mbah Kung, their grandfather. Alia was nervous, but she was also excited. *Mbah in the Javanese language means grandpa or grandma.

“How fun, we can play all afternoon. No one’s going to tell us to come home!” said Bagas. But Mbah Kung came to pick them up. They had to stop playing and go home at once. After only one day, Alia missed Mom.

Alia and Bagas had to get up early, even on the weekends. “Help me sweep the yard! Weekends are no excuse to be lazy,” Mbah Kung scolded.

Mbah Kung even made them take baths on the weekend. “Do we really have to take a bath?” Alia grumbled. Mom used to brush Alia’s hair and put it up with pins or ribbons. Now, Alia had to do all that herself. What a hassle!

“Come here, let me help you!” Mbah Kung said. Alia did as she was told. “But why is one of my pigtails higher than the other?” Alia complained. But Mbah Kung told her not to fuss over such small matters. Alia was upset! This made her miss Mom even more.

When Alia and Bagas climbed the guava tree, Mbah Kung scolded, “Hey, get down from there! You’ll fall!” “Don’t do this, don’t do that,” Alia mocked.

When it was time for lunch Mbah Kung cooked the same meal every day. Either vegetables with peanut sauce, stir fry, or vegetable stew. “Just eat, don’t be picky!” Mbah Kung said. Today, Alia and Bagas didn’t want to eat. When Mbah Kung went back to his room, they took their bikes and left.

They saw their neighbor Mbah Tum drying grain. Her movements made it seem like she was playing a game. Alia and Bagas wanted to try for themselves. “Even it out, back and forth!” Alia instructed Bagas.

However, Mbah Kung came to pick them up. “Why haven’t you two eaten? Eat first, then you can play!” Mbah Kung ordered. Alia and Bagas reluctantly went back home.

“I’m bored of eating vegetables and peanut sauce,” Bagas whispered. “Let’s cook for ourselves. We’ll put some vegetables in eggs, just like Mom does,” Alia said. “Yes!” Bagas agreed.

Alia prepared the ingredients. She peeled garlic and cut up vegetables. She ground some pepper. She added the vegetables to the eggs and mixed them together. She had just started to fry the egg batter, when Bagas called for her.

Bagas’ bicycle chain had come off. Alia helped him fix it. Suddenly, a strange smell wafted through the air. “Oh, no!’ Alia shrieked.

“The eggs are scorched!” Alia cried.

“The heat was too high! Never leave the stove when you’re cooking, it’s dangerous!” Mbah Kung scolded again. “What were you trying to make?” “Vegetable omelettes,” Alia answered. “I don’t want to eat vegetables with peanut sauce anymore,” Bagas added. Mbah Kung sighed and invited Alia to cook with him.

“Slice the carrots to the shape of matches,” ordered Mbah Kung. “Round cuts also work!” Alia said. “The garlic should be grounded,” Mbah Kung suggested. “Slicing them is easier,” said Alia. Alia and Mbah Kung kept arguing.

Finally, the vegetable omelettes were ready to be served. Would it taste like Mom’s cooking? “Bagas, let’s dig in!” Alia called. However, Bagas was nowhere to be seen.

“Bagas must have run away because you’re so strict, Mbah Kung,” said Alia quietly. Mbah Kung didn’t say anything.

Ring, ring! Bagas was back. “Are the omelettes ready? I don’t like hearing you two argue,” Bagas said.

Alia brought Bagas to the table to eat. But where was Mbah Kung? Why wasn’t he eating with them?

Alia went to look for Mbah Kung in his room. Mbah Kung was looking at a photo of Mom. His eyes were full of tears. It turns out that Alia wasn’t the only one who missed Mom.

They ate together in silence. “We all miss your mom’s cooking,” said Mbah Kung. “Yes. I miss when Mom reads to me, too,” Bagas added.

Mbah Kung read them stories. Mbah Kung brushed Alia’s hair. Mbah Kung also asked them to cook with him.​

When would Mom come home? She’d be happy to see that Alia and Bagas made a new friend, Mbah Kung.

title: Uh Oh, Pang Pang Is Up to Something
content:
BANGBANG, POW, BOOMWHOOSH, POP!Who's making all that noise?It's probably pang pang again. He's always up to something.

Alright, Just a pinch of this white flour, some water, and boil it all together. Abracadabra abracadabra, count to ten...done! Now I just need to pour it into this pan and light this fire...KOONG PANG KOONG PANG!

The noise startles a mother duck and her baby ducklings, who were out on a stroll.They all flee to a cave and hide.

*Eek eek! What is that noise?Is that a ghost?*The monkeys chatter as they scramble up the trees.

"Oh no, Mr. Tiger must be angry. I must leave before he gets too angry"Snakes frantically burrow into the ground, Ants scurry into their tunnels, Birds flock into the trees.

Pang Pang watches with glee as all the animals scurry away. He feels like king of the forest.With just a few ingredients, he could scare anyone.

"Grrr, I can't take this anymore! Let me just go and snatch his pot away right now!"growled Mr. Monkey. "Me neither.My baby sister ducklings are too scared to go anywhere because of that up-to-no-good- bear. We must put an end to all this." Mrs. Duck was furious.

Having had enough, the animals in the forest held a meeting to discuss what to do with Pang Pang.

The very next day, a group of baby moles dug a large hole in front of pang pang's house.

Then, everyone else got their drums, cymbals, flutes, trumpets, violins, guitars, and started to play very loudly in front of pang pang's house.

Pang pang, who couldn't concentrate, shouted from inside the house. "AAAARGJ what is all this noise about??"Pang pang burst out angrily, "AAAARGJ what is all this noise??"As soon as he stepped out, he fell straight into the hole the moles had dug. "AHHH!"

The animals cheered and jumped excitedly, "Hooray! we got him! No more of pang pang bothering us any longer. "

Now there was a wise old goat, who watched everything happen from a distance. When the cheering died down he cleared his throat and bleeted, "Everyone! Is this what you wish to be? A village that always fights with each other? Pang Pang! what do you think? Pang pang stops and thinks for a moment.

The animals approached pang pang one by one, "our kids were getting scared and couldn't sleep at night because of your tricks. the rest of us couldn't do anything without worrying. "

"And everyone look at pang pang! He's bruised all over. Does that make you feel better? Now that you got your revenge? "

If we continue to revenge one another and make ourselves uncomfortable, one day, our forest will not last. Don't you forget that. From now on, we must try to think of a better way to live peacefully together.

What do you think everyone? What do you think is the solution ?

title: Naughty Dog
content:
We are a family of four. I follow Chinku everywhere.

I have to look after Chinku. You see, I am older than him.

Sometimes Chinku is careless. It is my duty to guard the house.

We do everything together. We work together.

We play together.

We even share Ma’s scolding.

When Chinku is at school I help Ma. I keep the crows away from the papads.

Today Chinku will be my teacher. At last, I will learn something new.

I am a good doggy. I do not scare away cats.

Are you Chinku’s friend? Then you are my friend too.

Read the following action sentences. Which of these activities do you like to do? I like dancing. I like swimming. I like skipping. I like drawing.

I like cycling. I like climbing. Sometimes we say, "As faithful as a dog". This is because a dog always stays close to its master. If it goes far away or is lost, a dog always finds its way back home.

title: The Absent Boy
content:
“Rajib! Rajib!”Rajib hears someone call his name. When he lifts his head, he sees that he is lying in the bottom of a deep well. His mother is looking down at him and screaming his name.

“Mommy!” Rajib yells out in a panic. He takes deep breaths.“Babu, what’s wrong? Why do you look so frightened? Was it a nightmare?” Rajib’s mother asks.

Rajib looks around. He realizes he's in his bedroom. “Babu, it’s time for school. Wash up and come eat something.” His mother combs through his hair with her fingers, then walks towards the kitchen.

“Rajib! What's taking you so long?”

“Mom, is it true that I look like my grandfather?” asks Rajib.“Yes, your nose, ears, and mouth are like his,” she answers.“And did people tease grandfather?” he asks.“Not that I know of. Why do you ask?”she says.“No reason,” replies Rajib.

After breakfast, Rajib heads out to school, but he only makes it to the front of the schoolyard. Something makes him turn around. He goes back into his room and shuts the door. He spends the entire day in his room. When Rajib’s mother asks him why he isn’t at school, he says he feels unwell.

In the evening, Rajib finally leaves his room. He goes up to the terrace and stands there for a long time. The sun is setting. He feels like he is drowning. He holds his breath.

The next day, Rajib goes to school. But...

...he spends most of his time by a creek next to the school. He picks up small rocks and flings them across the surface of the water. As soon as he hears the last bell ring, he heads home.

In the evening, Rajib does his schoolwork. “Mom, when I’m older, I will grow my hair out,” he says. “Why do you want longer hair?” His mother asks. But Rajib doesn’t say anything.

Rajib starts skipping school.

Rajib's mother notices that he stands in front of the mirror for long periods of time. He sometimes pulls at his ears and twists them. Sometimes he pulls at his hair to try and cover his ears. When he's alone, she finds him staring off into space.

Every evening, Rajib goes up to the terrace and stands there until dark.

One day, Rajib’s brother comes to visit from Australia. He brings a gift for Rajib.

The brothers play video games late into the night. In one of the games, they enter a tunnel.Rajib’s brother holds Rajib’s hand. “Bhai, it’s pretty dark in here, are you scared?” he asks. “No, I only get scared when I’m at school...”

Rajib’s brother turns on the flashlight on his phone. Suddenly their enemies appear. Rajib is shocked. Their opponents are his schoolmates!“Nooo! How did you guys find me here?” Rajib screams.

“Bhai, what happened?” Rajib’s brother asks, worriedly. “Dai, these kids pull my ears and call me ‘rabbit.’ And that boy named Bhola over there, he makes me take my pants off whenever he finds me alone in the bathroom.” Rajib begins to tremble.

Rajib’s brother opens his mouth to speak but no words come out. Shaking his head, he finally manages to say, “This is horrible! My little brother is having such a hard time and I have been so far away.”He hugs Rajib and says to him, “But don’t worry, bhai. You no longer have to be afraid. I will go to your school first thing tomorrow."

"For now, come, let’s get these bad guys!"

Rajib and his brother fight in the tunnel. When they beat the enemies on screen, they celebrate.

The next day Rajib’s brother goes to school with him. Together they tell the teacher about all the bullying and mistreatment that Rajib has been enduring at school. The teachers call Rajib’s classmates into the office. “Sorry, Rajib. We won’t hurt you again,” they promise.

After that, Rajib goes to school regularly. A month later, his brother leaves for Australia. Every Saturday, Rajib and his brother meet online to play video games. While they play, they talk openly about their day and the good and bad times they experience.

Wonderful Wordsbabu - a term of endearment for a little child, especially for a little boy, in the Nepali languagebhai - younger brother in Nepali dai - older brother in Nepali

title: Grasshopper Speaks Up
content:
Grasshopper, Frog, and Cricket love to run and play in the green meadow every day.

One day, Grasshopper's friends are not feeling well and decide to stay home. Grasshopper does not think it is a big deal. He runs outside to play anyway.

But the next day, Grasshopper's friends are not in the meadow again. He looks everywhere for them, but they are nowhere to be found. Grasshopper decides to fly home alone.

On the way, he sees Cricket spraying chemicals on plants that are being grown for food. There are containers of empty chemicals floating in the river nearby.

Grasshopper thinks about stopping to greet his friend. But he is still upset that Cricket did not come to play, so he flies on.

A few days later, Cricket stops by to see Grasshopper. "Where have you been?" Grasshopper asks. "Why haven't you come to the meadow to play?" "Oh, I have a terrible stomachache and a headache. I can barely walk," Cricket says, moaning.

Grasshopper is worried for his friend. "You may have eaten something poisonous. Let's go to the doctor."Grasshopper helps his friend walk. But when they come to the river, Cricket is too weak to fly across.Grasshopper finds a stick to make a bridge. Cricket begins to walk across but slips!

"Help! I'm going to fall into the water!" Cricket cries.Grasshopper grabs hold of the stick to try to save Cricket."Hang on!" he shouts.

Cricket slips down the stick further. "I can't hold on for long." Grasshopper encourages Cricket to be strong. "Don't let go! There is something in the water below that might bite you."

Suddenly, the stick breaks! Grasshopper and Cricket fall down into the water. A giant frog leaps up, ready to swallow them both.

Just in time, Grasshopper shouts, "Stop, Frog! It is us, your friends!"Grasshopper and Cricket crawl onto a nearby lily pad.

"Oh, I did not realize it was you!" Frog says. "I have not been able to see well lately. What are you doing here?"Grasshopper replies, "We are going to the doctor. Cricket is very sick."

"Maybe I should come too," Frog says. "My eyes are bothering me, and my skin has a strange rash."

Grasshopper thinks he knows what is going on. He decides it is time to speak up. "Cricket, I am afraid the chemicals you sprayed on the plants are unhealthy for your food. And the containers that were dumped in the water have hurt Frog's eyes and skin."Cricket feels terrible for having caused so much trouble. "It's okay, Cricket," Frog says with a smile. "We will make it right. But first let's get to the doctor so we will all feel better!"

Once he is healthy again, Cricket cleans up the garbage and waste from the water. He learns new ways to care for his plants that do not use harmful chemicals.

More About the EnvironmentConservation International (CI) works with local communities and primary schools near the Pursat River and Tonle Sap Lake to raise awareness about environmental issues. CI provides information on waste control, pesticide use, wildlife protection, and environmental education so that communities can care for and use these valuable local water resources.

title: The Flower Hunt
content:
"Little Hummingbird, will you bring home some night-blooming jasmine for the nest?" Mother asked.

I went out to search for the night-blooming jasmine."Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the white lotus, Little Hummingbird," said Ladybug.That was not the flower I needed, so I flew along.

"Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the dahlia, Little Hummingbird." said Butterfly.That was not the flower I needed, so I flew along.

"Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the sunflower, Little Hummingbird," said Caterpillar.That was not the flower I needed, so I flew along.

"Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the ground lily, Little Hummingbird," said Bee.That was not the flower I needed, so I flew along.

"Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the poinsettia, Little Hummingbird," said Spider.That was not the flower I needed, so I flew along.

"Which flower is this, friend?" I asked. "It is the night-blooming jasmine, Little Hummingbird," said Firefly."Just what I needed!" I said happily. "Thank you, Firefly."

"Well done, my Little Hummingbird! Now our nest looks very pretty," said Mother.

title: The Black Forest is Dangerous
content:
The teacher opened a big map and said, "Today’s homework is to walk around the town. Do you think you can do this?" Doodoo raised his hand. "Teacher, can I go anywhere?"

"Yes! But remember! You cannot go to the dark forest because it is very DANGEROUS!" Ding dong~! the school bell rang. The children exclaimed and scattered away, except Doodoo.

Doodoo looked at the dark forest on the map. "Teacher said it is such an awful forest."

Doodoo smiled softly. "Then there must be something exciting waiting for me!"

Full of excitement, Doodoo rushed home to prepare for his journey. "I need a cloak to explore!" "Oh, I should take this pouch, too." "Also, these red balloons that I like !"

In the dark forest, the wind was making a whooshing sound. It was really creepy. Then, the wind blew fiercely and scared Doodoo. Woosh~ "Totto, let’s go!" Doodoo balled up his hands into fists and entered the black forest.

He took one step, then another...

Cough! Cough!

Cough! Cough! Cough! The forest was filled with dust. His nose tickled and his eyes got watery.

Then, somewhere, there was a fresh breeze. From a very, very big green tree. "Don’t worry, I can help you!"

The tree sucked in all the dust. Doodoo plopped down under the tree’s shadow. The air under the tree was very fresh.

"Thank you, Green Tree! I’ll plant more trees just like you."

The green tree seemed to be excited, so it started swaying and waving its leaves. Doodoo went back into the trail.

He took one step, and another...

buzz~! buzz~! "Buzz, buzz!" There was a bunch of mosquitos in the forest. buzz~! buzz~! "Ugh, go away!" The more he waved his arm, the more the mosquitos bit him.

Suddenly, he heard a little voice somewhere. "Please, help me!"

A baby monkey was crouching in the forest crying.

Doodoo had a great idea! Doodoo tied his cloak tightly between the trees and covered the baby monkey.

"Don’t worry. Now the mosquitos won’t bite you." Doodoo excitedly walked away.

He took one step, then another...

Suddenly, the ground started shaking, And bricks were falling down. The animal school collapsed! "What should I do?" The animals began to shout and stomp their feet.

"It’s ok. We can build it again!" Doodoo rolled up his sleeves and piled up the bricks one by one. Following Doodoo’s lead, animal friends started stacking the bricks too.

Doodoo decorated the school with red balloons. "Well, what do you think? It looks nice, doesn’t it?" His animal friends had a great big smile.

Doodoo also gave books as gifts. "Now, have fun with your friends at school. Alright?"

He took one step, then another...

Then finally, he was at the end of the forest. Finally, his friends gathered in front of the dark forest. "Wow, the dark forest has changed!" Doodoo proudly exclaimed. "The scary dark forest is nothing to be afraid of as long as you have courage. You can be brave too!" "Now… where shall I go next..."

Read a Book Today, Lead a Dream Tomorrow! Books International is an NGO specializing in picture books. We write, illustrate, and distribute picture books to children to read in their native languages. Our vision for this organization is to give children dreams of a hopeful future. Our stories also educate children on real-life issues and present-day situations. Books International aims to achieve equality for all children to access quality education.

title: Jimmy’s New Glasses
content:
It is a bright, sunny morning. Jimmy is up early. He is super excited about his first day at school.

Jimmy rushes to pack his bag. Then he dashes to get ready. His mom is making his favorite cheese sandwich for lunch.

In class, Jimmy sits all the way at the back. He squints and blinks, then rubs his eyes. “Why can’t I see the chalkboard properly?” he mumbles.

Jimmy moves to an empty desk in the front row. Mojo the Rabbit is sitting there alone. They begin talking and soon become friends.

Jimmy is curious about the object on Mojo’s face. “What is that thing on your face, Mojo?” he asks. “Oh, they are called glasses,” Mojo replies. “Glasses, wow! What do they do?” Jimmy asks. “Well, they help me see the world more clearly,” Mojo answers. “Does that make you look different from others?” asks Jimmy worriedly. “No, not at all. There is nothing wrong with wearing a pair of glasses,” says Mojo with a smile.

“Awesome! I think I might need glasses too,” Jimmy tells Mojo. Just then, their class teacher Miss Smith walks in. “Good morning, class,” she says. She turns around and begins writing on the chalkboard. “Please copy this in your books.”

Jimmy squints at the chalkboard. The letters seem too small and too blurry. “I cannot see the chalkboard clearly, but I am afraid to tell Miss Smith,” he whispers to Mojo. However, Mojo is eager to help Jimmy overcome his fear.

Mojo raises his hand and calls out, “Excuse me, Miss. Could you come here please?” Miss Smith stops writing and turns around. “Yes, Mojo. What happened?” she asks. “Jimmy wants to say something, but he is nervous,” says Mojo.

“What is wrong, Jimmy?” asks Miss Smith. “The writing on the chalkboard is too small for me to see,” says Jimmy nervously. “Aha, just that? Don’t worry, Jimmy. I will write a bit bigger for you,” says Miss Smith. “Never be afraid to ask for help. Nobody will growl at you or tease you,” she adds.

After school, Jimmy’s mom comes to pick him up. Jimmy tells her about not being able to see the chalkboard clearly. Miss Smith is listening too, and she nods her head. “I suggest you take Jimmy for an eye exam,” she says. Jimmy’s mom agrees. “Don’t worry, my boy. You will be all right,” she says to him.

The next morning, Jimmy and his mom visit the eye doctor. The doctor does some tests. She advises Jimmy to wear glasses so he can see clearly. He has a good time picking a pair of frames. Blue, yellow, or red? There are so many choices!

The following day, Jimmy goes to school with his new glasses. “Wow! You look even smarter in glasses,” says Mojo. “Thank you, Mojo. I got the idea from you though,” Jimmy replies. “The beautiful world seems much clearer now.” He laughs, giving Mojo a high five.

title: Abdul Kalam: A Lesson for My Teacher
content:
While the author, illustrator, and publisher of this book encourage and support translation of this work into other languages, they request that substantive changes to the text and art be kept to a minimum.

I lived on the Mosque Street in Rameswaram, a city famous for its Shiva temple. Every evening on my way home from the mosque, I would linger near the temple.

I always felt like a stranger there, as the temple goers stared suspiciously at me. They probably wondered what a Muslim boy was doing in front of a temple.

The truth was that I loved to listen to the rhythmic chanting of the mantras, though I never understood a word. There was a strange magic in them.

Of course, something else led me there. My best friend, Ramanadha Sastry, was the son of the head priest. He would sit beside his father at this hour, reciting hymns. Ram would steal a smiling glance at me from time to time.

At school, Ram and I always sat together on the first bench of our classroom. We were like brothers. However, being a Hindu priest’s son, he wore a sacred thread, while my white cap marked me as a Muslim.

One day, when we were in the fifth standard, a new teacher came to our class. He looked strict. He went around the class tapping his cane on his palm and stopped before us.

"You, the one in the white cap," he shouted. "How dare you sit beside the temple priest’s son! Go sit on the last bench." I felt hurt. With tears in my eyes, I picked up my books and shifted to the last row.

Ram and I wept together silently after school. We thought we would not be allowed to be friends anymore.

When I reached home that day my father looked at me and asked: "Were you crying... What’s wrong son?" I recounted the whole incident to my father, while Ram told his family the same story.

Early the next morning, Ram came running to our house and said: "Father has asked you to come to our house immediately." I was terrified. I thought I was in for some more trouble.

We hurried back to Ram’s house. My heart skipped a beat when I saw our new teacher standing there.

"In the light of our discussion, apologise to Kalam here," said Ram’s father with a stern face. I could not believe what I had just heard! The head priest was asking the teacher to apologise to me?

"No child is less than another in God’s eyes," Ram father said. "It is your duty as a teacher to help students live in harmony in spite of the differences in their background. You can no longer teach in this school."

Our teacher immediately asked me to forgive him. He hugged me and said: "I am sorry, Kalam. I have learnt an important lesson in life today."

Ram’s father saw that the teacher sincerely regretted his behaviour and permitted him to continue teaching.

From that day on, Ram and I sat together proudly on the front bench. We have remained the best of friends ever since.

title: Our Superhero Edhi Baba
content:
This Monday morning every student was ready to present their favorite superhero with the best superpower they could find. The teacher was so happy to see the enthusiasm in every child. She organized the jumping students and started the presentations.

After the presentations of Superman and Spider-man, the Hulk and many others, came Talha and Maha, two students who were dressed in gray shirts. Everyone was wondering what their super power was, and began listening to their poem.

Little Edhi saw his mother giving to the needy. She thought she wouldn’t care.

But he started giving every day, whatever he could spare.

His heart grew a little bigger every day, and eventually, he became a superhero with an incredibly large heart.

His heart was so big that it had room for everyone in need, regardless of their skin color.

He had the fastest car, white and shiny, to heal every injury no matter how tiny.

Ehdi Baba was the kindest man. We follow what was his plan. Help and donate is what we do. We have the superpower of big heart, you can get it, too!

Indeed a BIG HEART is the most wonderful super power we have been looking for…. The teacher smiled, the while class clapped for the lovely EHDI BABA poem and donated with whatever they could spare.

Notes for parents/teachers: Late Abdul Sattar Edhi had a habit of charity since childhood; his mother made him donate an amount of money from his daily allowance to the needy. This habit flourished and made Edhi a world renowned humanitarian from Pakistan. Superheroes have big hearts. Sharing makes your heart big. Sharing with a person in need makes it even bigger. Sharing with a person you do not like or you do not agree with makes your heart the biggest. Help, share and donate to be a superhero. There is an ambulance service by Edhi Foundation which has a network of ambulances all over Pakistan. It facilitates patients in need to reach their destinations.

title: The Garden in the Wardrobe
content:
Ma’s Jamdani wardrobe is a garden where hundreds of flowers grow and thousands of stars shine.

Ma shows me the saris and tells me about the patterns. “These patterns are woven out of cotton thread by the Jamdani weavers who live in a village by the river. There, water in the air makes the cotton soft. First they make the fine thread. Then, they sit at giant looms and use their hands and feet, one thread at a time, to weave a sari from the flower patterns that grow in their minds.'”“Ma, how do they remember all these flowers?” “Because it is impossible to forget something you love.”

Ma tells me what the patterns mean. “This one is a sandesh, a type of sweetmeat. And this one is a bitter gourd.” Ma points out the shapes woven onto the border of the sari.“EEEE! Why would you want bitter gourd on your sari, Ma?”“Because bitter things are good for you, my darling.”

“What is this pattern Ma?”“This one is special. It is called a chandrahar, a moon necklace. It is very precious because it took the light of many moons to make it. I wear it when I am happy with myself. This Jamdani reminds me that good things take time.”

My Ma says that many things will change as I grow up, but her love and the Jamdani garden will always stay the same. She says when I grow up, she will give me her Jamdani garden. This is my heritage, and I must keep it safe.

NoteThe Jamdani is one of the most complicated handwoven fabrics in the world. It is made completely by hand using only natural materials. A single sari can take weeks to finish, depending on the difficulty of the design, which is usually woven from memory. The designs are geometric forms inspired by nature. The loom is worked by two weavers, a master and an apprentice, who pass the needle back and forth as the master calls out the pattern instructions. This craft is recognized as an intangible heritage of Bangladesh.

Wonderful Wordsjamdani - a beautiful, traditional woven fabric made on a pit-loom powered by two weavers who pass the thread back and forth following patterns which the Master Weaver sings out.chandrahar - a pattern used in weaving. Jamdani weavers use this pattern to represent a necklace made of moons.

title: The Pitha Book
content:
My favorite book is the Pitha Book , written by Ma. Even though I can't read, I look at the pictures and remember when she made each rice cake.

BHAPA PITHA (The snow clouds) This rice cake means that winter is here. When Ma makes this cake the steam mixes with the fog and the house turns into a gur cloud. We wait eagerly as she serves the hot cakes directly into our palms.

PATISHAPTA (Baby in a Blanket)Whenever I am not feeling well, Ma makes this rice cake to lift my spirits. She says this pitha, which is a soft roll stuffed with sweet cream, is full of comfort and makes even the hardest days better, like cuddling up in a well-loved blanket.

CHITA RUTI PITHA (The Fishing Net)This pitha is like a fishing net. It is 70 %air and 30 %rice flour, but 10 0% delicious. Ma makes this pitha when my sister comes to visit from college. She serves it with chicken and potatoes and there are never any leftovers.

NAKSHI PITHA (Happiness)Ma made this pitha for Bhaiya's wedding. It is very pretty and looks like the designs on Ma's sari. She let me help her make the patterns, and told me that each pitha would add a year of sweetness to my brother’s life. I stayed up all night, making pitha after pitha.

NotePithas are traditional rice cakes which come in many strange shapes and textures - wrinkly, curly, round, soft, hard, sweet, savory, salty. Some are soaked in sweet syrup. Some are dry and crispy. Some are salty and spicy. Some are cold, and some are steaming hot. Pithas are a favorite snack and dessert all across Bangladesh. There are more than 10 0d ifferent types.

Wonderful WordsGur - molasses

title: The Caterpillar’s Friend
content:
One beautiful, sunny morning, a tiny egg resting on a leaf cracked open. Out came a tiny caterpillar!

The tiny caterpillar was very hungry. She at leaves and berries and grew quickly. But her branch was lonely. So she decided to go in search of a friend to play with.

In the garden near her tree, Caterpillar saw a bee. He was very busy collecting pollen to turn into honey.

"Hello, there!" she said. "Would you like to be my friend?""I am too busy to play," the bee buzzed. "I have to make a lot of honey today!"

Next, Caterpillar met a dung beetle. He was busy rolling a giant ball of manure, and singing as he worked, "Rolling, rolling, rolling, I've got to keep on rolling!" "Hello! Would you like to play ball with me?" Caterpillar asked.

But the dung beetle did not even stop. "Rolling, rolling. I've got to keep rolling. No time to play!"After the beetle rolled past with his stinky ball, Kate decided she would not mind looking for a different friend.

She soon heard someone crying. She found a young spider crying so many tears, he had made a lake of sadness around him. "What is wrong?" Caterpillar asked.

"I fell out of my web, and can't get back," he cried. "I want my mommy!"Caterpillar comforted the little spider. "Climb on my back and I will take you home."

Mama Spider was so happy to see Little Spider again and gave him a big eight-legged hug. "I am so glad you are OK!" she said. "Who is your new friend?"Caterpillar was so delighted to realize she had found a friend at last.

The two new friends had a wonderful time playing together. But soon, it was time for Caterpillar to make a cocoon.

After working hard to make her cocoon, she said goodnight to her friend. Spider promised to watch over her as she slept and keep other insects away.

Little Spider and Mama Spider even spun extra web to protect Caterpillar.

For several days, Caterpillar slept. Finally, the cocoon began to shiver and shake."Caterpillar, is that you?" Spider yelped in surprise.

His friend had become a butterfly! She may have changed, but their friendship was still the same.

The End

title: Pohela Boishakh
content:
"Do you know what day it is tomorrow, Asha?" Apu asked."I think it’s Tuesday" replied Asha."Yes, it’s Tuesday, but it’s also April 14 th, the Bengali New Year!""How come it’s tomorrow and not in December?""Because tomorrow is the start of Boishakh , the first season of the Bengali calendar. Did you know that Bangladesh is the only country in the world that has six seasons?"

That evening, Apu and I went to the Art College where the students were busy m,aking HUGE figures of animals. There was a giant tiger made of bamboo and paper, a gigantic fish and an elephant the size of a house! Many students were preparing owl masks and painting clay pots. "We are getting ready for tomorrow’s Mangal Shobhajatra ," one of Apu’s friends explained."This year, the parade is about unity and we are making different animals to show them living together in peace. Tomorrow we will drive them down the roads of the university!"

In the morning, Apu and I woke up very early and walked to Ramna Park. As the sun began to rise, the choir under the banyan tree began to sing…"Esho Hey Boishakh, Esho, Esho…""Come O Boishakh, Come, Come…"Apu explained that this is a song written by the poet Rabindranth Tagore to welcome the first sunbeams of the new year.

Next, we went to watch the parade. I saw the giant fish and the enormous elephant floating happily above the crowds. Everyone was dressed in bright new clothes and there were flowers everywhere. I made sure not to get lost in the crowd as we slowly followed the huge tiger.

When we came home, Ammu and Baba were waiting for us. They were hungry!"Hurry, hurry, the ilish fish is ready and the panta bhat awaits you!""What is panta bhat, Ammu?" I asked. "Panta bhat is rice that we bring from the old year into the new. Yesterday I left the cooked rice to soak in water overnight and today it has a special taste. Together with the fried ilish, it is the perfect meal to start the Bengali New Year!" said Ammu. I sat down with Ammu, Baba, and Apu and thought to myself, this is going to be a very good year. Esho Hey Boishakh, Esho, Esho.

NoteThe Bengali calendar is split into 6 seasons. The first month, Grisho , starts on April 14 which is known as Pohela Boishakh, or Bengali New Year, in Bangladesh. On this day, there is a grand parade in Dhaka and Chattogram prepared by the art college students. This celebration is listed by UNESCO as a Cultural Heritage of Humanity. It is a celebration of harvest, love, friendship, and family.

Wonderful WordsBoishakh - The first season of the Bengali calendar.Mangal Shobhajatra - Also known as The Procession of Well-Being, is an annual parade held on the morning of the Bengali New Year. Ilish - Another name for the Hilsha fish, related to herring.Panta bhat - A name for rice that is brought from the old year into the Bengali new year.

title: Animal Hide-and-Seek
content:
Rhino is very shy. She always plays by herself around the lake. Gecko decides to play a trick on her. He asks all the other animals to join him.

"Rhino!" Gecko calls. "Do you want to play hide-and-seek with us? We will decide who hides first with rock-paper-scissors."

The other animals know that Rhino can only make paper with her big feet. They all make scissors on purpose. Rhino will have to be the seeker.

The animals start looking for places to hide. They ask each other, "Where should we hide so Rhino can’t find us?"

Rhino starts counting. "Five… ten… fifteen…" When she’s done counting to a hundred, she opens her eyes. "Where is everyone?" she wonders. "How will I find them now?"

Monkey had climbed into a tree. Rhino is overjoyed."Monkey, you have a long tail!" she calls. "I can see it clearly!" Squirrel had hidden in a tree's trunk. Rhino smiles. "Squirrel, I can see your fluffy tail!"

Rabbit is hiding nervously inside a cave. Nearby, Hedgehog had covered herself with flowers. Rhino finds them immediately. "Hedgehog and Rabbit! How could you both hide in such obvious places?" Rhino giggles.

Snail is crawling slowly under a leaf.

Parrot hides confidently on a tree branch. But his feathers are so bright that spotting him is easy. Rhino has found more than half the animals!

Silly Deer hides among the leafless trees. Giant Bear tries to hide behind the rocks.Rhino laughs out loud. "I can see where you both are hiding!"

Turtle hides in her shell, pretending to be a rock. Frog hides among some bushes across from her. But Rhino sees them both.

Finally, only Gecko remains hidden. Rhino cannot find him anywhere. The other animals tease, "You will have to look really hard now!"

Soon, Rhino has searched for Gecko everywhere. Her feet are worn out!

Rhino sits down, trying not to cry. The other animals start to feel bad. "Do you need a hint?" they ask. "No, I don’t need anyone’s help. Gecko might be good at hiding, but I will find him soon!"

At last, Rhino bows her head and stares into the lake. Suddenly, she cries out, "Gecko! I've found you!" Gecko grins. "I hid right on top of your horn! Pretty genius, right?"

Rhino laughs. She no longer feels shy. "Now it’s my turn to hide, and all of you will have to find me. I already know where I’ll hide!"

title: Nima’s First Day of School
content:
Nima is not happy today. Father buys her a pair of shoes. But she is still not happy.

Mother buys her a bag. But she is still not happy.

Nima is going to school today. But she does not want to go! Sister gives her an exercise book. But Nima still doesn’t want to go to school.

Brother brings her a book. But she is not happy. "I won’t go to school," Nima cries. Mother and father laugh.

Her parents take her to school. Nima walks as slowly as she can.

"It’s only for today. I won’t go tomorrow," Nima thinks as she walks.

At school, there are so many new friends. Now Nima is happy. She wants to go to school every day!

title: The Lantern Girl
content:
Nora and her friends headed home after their Qur’an class at the mosque. Nora urged her friends to take a different path. “It’s closer that way,” said Nora. “And pass by the haunted house?” Devon exclaimed. “Why don’t we take our usual path home?” asked Silva.

“It looks like it’s going to rain soon. We have to get home quickly,” said Nora. Devon and Silva agreed but Nora knew they were scared. Every time there was a noise they immediately huddled closer to Nora. Then ...

… Nora’s torch fell and went out! Everyone was startled. Devon and Silva immediately ran away, scared. “Hey, wait!” shouted Nora. But they kept running away.

Nora walked home alone. Ah, if only they had electricity in their village. Was there any other way to light up the path?

Back home, Mom was cooking. Seeing the flames gave Nora an idea.

“Mom, can I light my torch with the flames?” asked Nora. Even though she was confused, Mom nodded. “Why do you need a torch inside the house?” asked Mom. “I want to put it out front to light the path home,” Nora explained.

“Wow, that’s a good idea,” Mom replied. “Let’s try it.” Nora and Mom tied the torch tightly to a bamboo pole. The front of Nora’s house immediately became brighter. Nora was happy.

However, a gust of wind made the flames of the torch sway back and forth. Lightning struck in the distance.

The wind grew stronger. Mom and Nora hurried back inside the house. Nora was anxious. What about the torch? Would the flames survive?

The flames went out. Nora was disappointed. Her idea of using a torch didn’t work. “I need to find another way,” she thought.

Nora could feel the wind blowing through the window. Strangely, the flames of the lamp didn’t go out. Nora realized that the glass of the lamp protected the flame from the wind. “Aha, I can use the lamp to replace the torch!” she proclaimed.

Dad helped Nora install the lamp. They waited to see what would happen to the flame. Success! Even though the wind was blowing, the flame in the lamp was still burning.

Pitter… Patter… rain! Nora hurriedly grabbed an umbrella. She went outside again to make sure the lamp was safe. Oh no, the cool raindrops hit the hot glass of the lamp and caused it to shatter! The flame immediately went out. Nora had to come up with a new plan. What could protect the lamp from the rain?

What could Nora use? A pot lid? No, Mom needed the lid to the pot for cooking. The bamboo tray? No, Mom needed the tray to separate the rice grains from their husks.

What about a banana leaf? No, that wouldn’t work. A gust of wind would tear the banana leaf.

Nora tried a used can. Oh no, the lamp was completely covered. Not only did the light not shine through, but the flame was also starting to go out. Nora looked around again to see what she could use.

Aha! There was an old pot lid. The lid had dents and holes in it. Nora was sure she could use this pot lid. She just needed to fix it a bit.

Nora covered the holes on the pot lid with used plastic bags. She painted the pot lid to make it look pretty.

Now the pot lid was ready to be used. “The lid has to be straight, and the knot has to be tight,” Mom instructed.

They erected a pole and attached the lamp to it. “Hopefully the lamp will be safe, and the flame won’t go out again,” said Nora.

“Whoa, this is so cool!” exclaimed Devon. “Let’s make one of our own,” said Silva. “Yes, let’s light up our village,” urged Nora.

The news of the lamp in front of Nora’s house began to spread. A lot of people were interested in following in Nora’s footsteps. Soon, lamp poles were erected in front of several houses in the village.

Now, the streets in Nora’s village weren’t as dark. Even though there was no electricity, the lamps lit up all the paths and made the night much brighter.
